reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Wednesday in late August. The kind of day nobody writes songs about. The summer is winding down but not gone, the light is starting to slant differently in the evenings, and there's nothing particularly to celebrate or survive. Just a regular day in a regular week.

When I was drinking, I hated days like this. They felt like filler between the weekends I was actually alive for. I couldn't sit inside an ordinary Wednesday without needing to sand the edges off it. The whole architecture of my life was built around escaping the middle of the week. What I've come to understand, slowly, is that the middle of the week is where a life actually gets built. Not in the highlight reel. In the reps. The morning coffee I remember drinking. The workout I showed up for even though nobody would've known if I skipped. The text back to a friend. The dinner I cooked instead of ordered.

Durant's line — really Aristotle's — sounds like a productivity slogan until you've watched your own life get shaped by what you did on the Wednesdays. Sobriety isn't the big moments. It's the accumulation of ordinary hours you stayed present for. That's the whole trick. Today is one of those hours. Don't waste it wishing it were a weekend.
reflection.meditation: Where in today can I stop waiting for something better and just be here?

affirmations: I am building a life in the small hours, not just the big ones.
Today I show up for the ordinary parts of my day without needing to escape them.
I am someone who can sit inside a regular Wednesday and call it enough.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a day that doesn't require anything dramatic from me. I'm grateful for the coffee this morning, the clear head to drink it with, and the fact that I no longer have to piece together what I said last night. Eleven years ago I couldn't have imagined being grateful for a quiet Wednesday. Now I know it's the whole point.
gratitude.closing: One ordinary day at a time. That's the work.
